# Behavioral Specification for AES Control Module

## 1. Scope

This module is the main sequencing and gating logic for the AES block. It tracks register-access activity, decides when to start a cipher operation, controls acceptance of cipher results, applies output back-pressure, and performs key/data clear operations. It does not implement the AES algorithm itself.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

On reset, the module shall:

- Enter an idle state.
- Report that it is idle.
- Report that the input data path is ready to accept a new input block.
- Report that the output data path does not yet contain valid result data.
- Report that it is not stalled.
- Clear all pending input-block, new-key, and output-read tracking state.

## 3. Operating Modes

The module shall support two operating modes:

- **Automatic mode**: The module shall automatically start the cipher operation whenever a complete input block is available and the module is idle. A complete input block is defined as all four input data registers having been written. The order of writes does not matter.
- **Manual mode**: The module shall not automatically start a cipher operation when input data is written. It shall instead wait for a start request. A start request shall be consumed only when the corresponding block operation is actually accepted for processing.

In manual mode, the module shall not stall the cipher output due to unread previous result data. New output data may overwrite previous output data regardless of whether it has been read.

## 4. Input Data Tracking and Block Start

The module shall monitor writes to the four input data registers at any time, including while another operation is in progress. The order of writes does not matter. Once all four registers have been written, the module shall consider a complete input block to be pending.

While a complete input block is pending, the module shall report that the input path is not ready. After the block is consumed by the cipher core, the module shall clear the pending-input state and report that the input path is ready again.

When a block operation is started:

- In automatic mode, a pending input block shall be sufficient to start the operation without any start request.
- In manual mode, a start request shall be required in addition to the pending input block.

The module shall not consider a block operation started until the cipher core accepts it. A start request shall be cleared only when the operation is accepted, subject to the decryption-key-generation exception described below.

## 5. Initial Key Tracking

The module shall monitor writes to the eight initial-key registers. The order of writes does not matter. A new key shall be considered complete once all eight key registers have been written.

Initial-key register writes shall only be forwarded to the key registers while the module is idle. A pending-new-key indication shall be cleared when decryption key generation is performed, or when the key registers are cleared.

## 6. Decryption Key Generation

When a decryption operation is requested and a new initial key is pending, the module shall first cause the cipher core to generate the decryption key before starting the actual block operation.

During decryption key generation:

- The pending input block must not be consumed.
- No output data must be accepted or written.
- The pending-new-key indication shall be cleared after key generation completes.
- In manual mode, the start request shall remain pending across the key-generation phase and shall be consumed only when the actual block operation starts.

After decryption key generation completes, the module shall proceed with the originally pending block operation using the same input data. If the pending block was started in automatic mode, it shall start automatically after key generation. If it was started in manual mode, the still-pending start request shall now initiate it.

If a decryption operation is requested and no new key is pending, no key-generation phase shall be performed.

## 7. Cipher Result Acceptance and Output Back-Pressure

The module shall wait for the cipher core to complete the current operation.

For a normal block operation, the module shall accept the cipher result only when the output data registers can safely be written:

- In manual mode, the result may always be accepted, regardless of whether previous output data has been read.
- In automatic mode, the result may be accepted only if there is no valid previous output data, or if all four output data registers have been read.

If the cipher core produces a result while the module cannot safely accept it, the module shall hold the result, refrain from overwriting the output data registers, and assert the stall indication. It shall accept the result once the condition is resolved.

When a result is accepted, the module shall:

- Write the output data registers.
- Set the output-valid indication.
- Return to idle so that a pending next input block can be started.

## 8. Output Data Read Tracking

The module shall monitor reads from the four output data registers. The order of reads does not matter.

Once all four output data registers have been read, the output-valid indication shall be cleared. If new output data is written in the same cycle that the last output register is read, the output-valid indication shall remain set, because the output data registers now contain new valid data.

## 9. Clear Operations

The module shall support clearing of input data, output data, and key material.

### 9.1 Input Data Clear

A data-in clear request shall:

- Discard any pending input block.
- Clear the input data registers.
- Cause the input path to become ready.
- Clear the data-in clear request.

This operation may be performed without waiting for cipher-core completion.

### 9.2 Output Data Clear

An output-data clear request shall:

- Clear the output data registers.
- Clear the output-valid indication.
- Clear the output-data clear request.

The module shall not consider the output-data clear complete until the cipher core has completed its part of the clear operation.

### 9.3 Key Clear

A key-clear request shall:

- Clear all initial key registers.
- Cause all key material in the cipher core to be cleared.
- Clear the pending-new-key indication.
- Clear the key-clear request.

The module shall not consider the key clear complete until the cipher core has completed its part of the clear operation.

### 9.4 Simultaneous Clear Requests

If key clear and output-data clear are requested together, the module shall perform both clear operations before returning to idle. If a data-in clear is also requested, it may be performed while the key/output clear operation is still being completed.

## 10. Prioritization Between Start and Clear Requests

If a start condition and a clear request are asserted while the module is idle, the start condition shall be handled first. The clear request shall remain pending and be serviced after the current operation has completed.

While an operation is already in progress, newly asserted clear requests shall remain pending until the operation finishes and the module returns to idle.

## 11. Status Indications

The module shall provide the following status behavior:

- **Idle**: Asserted when the module has no block operation or clear operation in progress.
- **Input ready**: Asserted when no complete input block is pending. Deasserted when all four input data registers have been written. Reasserted when the input block is consumed or cleared.
- **Output valid**: Asserted when the output data registers contain valid cipher result data. Remains asserted until all four output registers have been read or until output data is cleared.
- **Stall**: Asserted when a cipher result is available but cannot be accepted because previous output data has not been read. This shall never be asserted in manual mode.

The module shall never set the start request or the clear request bits; it may only clear them once the corresponding operation has been accepted or completed.
